List of Questions for ORAL   ANSWERS

Damage to Kirandul-Visakhapatnam
rail track due to overloading
*341. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY:  Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the 472
kilometers long rail track from Kirandul to
Visakhapatnam is in danger of heavy
damage due to overloading of iron ores in
goods trains;
(b) whether some trains were recently
cancelled due to damage to the tracks;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the amount lost due to such
cancellation;
(e) the reasons for not taking prompt
action;
(f) whether the geologists have also
expressed fear about this track;
(g) if so, Government’s response
thereto; and
(h) the steps being taken by
Government to improve the situation?
Threat from Atmospheric Brown
Cloud
*342. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO:  Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Atmospheric Brown Cloud (ABC), a
terminology generally used for the
enormous blanket of pollution comprising
ash, acids, etc., reduces the chances of
monsoon rains substantially in the
subcontinent thereby causing potential
threat to the agricultural harvests;
(b) if so, the measures taken/proposed
to be taken by Government to tackle the
threat;
(c) whether any study to assess its
impact on our country has been carried
out;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

107
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Quality of fruits and vegetables
supplied through Mother
Dairy outlets
*343. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. VIJAY MALLYA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the quality of vegetables
and fruits particularly onions and potatoes
supplied through the Mother Dairy outlets
in Delhi is inferior;
(b) whether any check is exercised by
the senior officers of his Ministry on the
officials of the organization responsible for
procurement;
(c) if so, at what level and whether any
irregularities/corruption in the procurement
have come to the light; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken to ensure reasonable good quality of
vegetables and fruits at reasonable prices
are made available through Mother Dairy
outlets in the State?
Leprosy patients in the country
†*344. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 62 per cent
of the world’s leprosy patients are in our
country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
largest number of such patients are there in
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh Orissa, Madhya
Pradesh and West Bengal;
(c) whether there is no qualitative
change in its present status despite the
leprosy eradication programme of
Government; and
(d) if so, the details of the existing
number of Leprosy patients and their
condition, State-wise and the details of
action taken by Government in this regard?
Venture capital fund for dairy and
poultry industry
*345. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have launched
a new NABARD-sponsored venture capital
fund for dairy and poultry industry with
corpus of Rs. 25 crores for three years;
(b) if so, whether Government would
ensure that provision of its micro-credit to
individual entrepreneurs, unemployed
youths, etc. percolates  to tribals and other
deprived sections of the society for their
gainful employment; and
(c) whether the backward and tribal
districts of Chhattisgarh and Yavatmal in
Maharashtra would be identified for
selective operaton of this scheme for the
year 2007, through NGOs or cooperative
societies functioning in such districts?
Assistance to Madhya Pradesh for
fishery development
†*346. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to refer to
answer to Unstarred Question1056 given
in the Rajya Sabha on the 2nd December,
2005 and state:
(a) whether the Government of
Madhya Pradesh has made a proposal
for sanctioning Rs. 52.49 lakhs for

108
development of fishery in reservoirs under
construction and constructed under the
Narmada Valley Development Project; and
(b) if so, by when the said amount would
be provided to the State?
Gauge conversion in north-eastern
region
*347. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) the names of rail lines that are under
conversion from metre gauge to broad gauge;
(b) the names of metre gauge lines that
are not under such conversion;
(c) whether in the north-eastern region
rail lines are mostly in metre-gauge and due
to this reason the goods are subjected to
frequent loading and unloading for
transportation outside the region causing
additional financial burden and this also
consumes a lot of time; and
(d) if so, the steps contemplated to
overcome these problems?
Indian Public Health Standards
*348. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:  Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the firstever
draft of the Indian Public Health Standards,
to have uniform guidelines to provide
quality healthcare in the country, has been
released by his Ministry recently;
(b) whether it is a part and parcel of the
National Rural Health Mission inaugurated
by the Prime Minister recently; and
(c) the minimum functional grade
prescribed for community health centres?
Mangrove forests
*349. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) the area of mangrove forests in the
country in acres, State-wise;
(b) the details of mangrove forests and
their locations specifically in Andhra
Pradesh;
(c) whether Government extends
protection to mangrove forests; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Programme for checking infant and
maternal mortality
*350. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Orissa
Government proposes to launch a new
programme with the assistance of World
Bank to check the high infant and maternal
mortality rate in the State;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the State Government also
proposes to raise its sanitation standards
and improve other health-care facilities; and
(d) if so, the details thereof indicating
the action plan of the Centre to help this
backward region to achieve these laudable
goals?
Deficient forest cover in Punjab,
Haryana, U.P., etc.
*351. SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS
KAUR: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Punjab, Haryana, UP and

109
other parts of northern India, being mainly
agricultural areas, are markedly deficient in
Forest-Tree-Cover (FTC);
(b) whether declining prices of wood in
the context of free import of wood under
OGL presents added disincentive to farm-
forestry;
(c) if so, whether with the twin
objectives of increasing Forest-Tree-Cover
(FTC) and generating viable employment
opportunities, the Government of Punjab
and other State Governments have
requested the Centre to provide incentives
to farm-forestry while imposing
countervailing duties on import of wood
and wood products; and
(d) if so, what is Government’s response
thereto?
Ticketing system at Bangalore City
railway station
*352. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken to increase the
number of reservation and other ticket
issuing counters for various trains departing
from Bangalore City railway station;
(b) whether there is any proposal to
introduce IT enabled ticketing system at
the station; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Production and export of horticulture
items
*353. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have approved
a Centrally-Sponsored Scheme on
Technology Mission for the Integrated
Development of Horticulture in North East,
Sikkim, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal
Pradesh and Uttaranchal for enhancement
of assistance of components of TMNE at
par with National Horticulture Mission
(NHM) to help a large number of farmers,
entrepreneurs and exporters;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether any road map has been
drawn to boost production and export of
horticulture items in the above States?
Policy for purchase of antibiotics
*354. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to purchase antibiotics only from public
sector manufacturers, instead of through
market, using open tender route;
(b) whether it is a fact that the
distributors are purchasing antibiotics at
very low rates from PSUs and supplying
them to Government hospitals at the rate
contracts offered by the PSUs;
(c) whether Government’s directive on
purchasing antibiotics only from PSUs
violates an Andhra Pradesh High Court
order; and
(d) if the answers to above parts be in
the affirmative, the action Government
propose to take to remedy the situation?
Implementation of NAIS
*355. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the States and Union Territories

110
where National Agricultural Insurance
Scheme (NAIS) is not implemented and
the reasons thereof;
(b) the details regarding the premium
income the claims settled and the farmers
benefited during 2003-04, 2004-05 and
2005-06 till today;
(c) whether it is a fact that many past
claims of Gujarat and Maharashtra have
not been settled till today inspite of many
representations;
(d) whether it is also a fact that the rate
of premium on cotton is very high
compared to other items; and
(e) the details of items covered under
the scheme and the future plans to expand
the areas and cover more items especially
in drought prone States?
Decrease in agricultural production
in Andhra Pradesh
*356. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
production of some of the agricultural
products such as foodgrains, oilseeds,
sugarcane, jute etc. in Andhra Pradesh has
come down gradually during the last five
years, causing a serious concern;
(b) if so, what are Government’s plans
to revitalize the agriculture sector,
especially in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) the manner in which State has
benefited under the Macro Management
Programme; and
(d) the area in hectares of the State
covered under drip and sprinkler irrigation?
Assistance to FPIs
†*357. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of financial assistance
provided to Food Processing Industries
(FPI) during the last three years under the
plan development scheme by the Central
Government; State-wise;
(b) the details of the efforts made by
the Central Government for the
establishment, modernisation and
upgradation of food processing industry
units in the country especially in Andhra
Pradesh; and
(c) the details of food processing units
established/modernised during the last three
years in the State as a result of these efforts,
district-wise?
Allocations to Ayurvedic System of
Medicine
†*358. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
the National Policy, 10 per cent of the total
allocated amount should be allotted to
Ayurvedic System of Medicine;
(b) if not, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the total
allocated amount was only two per cent
during the previous years; and
(d) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the percentage of average amount allocated
for Ayurvedic System of Medicine every
year since 2004?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

*359. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether process for finalizing New
Pharmaceutical Policy is on the anvil;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
change the present methods of fixing prices
of drugs;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether there is any proposal to
allow the drug companies to fix the prices

Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY

take any initiative to standardize treatment

hospitals in the country;

and
